THE METHOD / VERSION 0.1

A measurement.
Not a prophecy.

01

Measure a distribution

Each daily window is represented as a distribution across a fixed topic taxonomy. A changing distribution means the observed event record has changed. It is not a direct measurement of the state of the world.

Source counts and coverage are shown separately so changes in reporting are not mistaken for changes in events.

02

Keep the reference explicit

Historical displacement compares the selected day's topic mix with a frozen reference or the previous 30 comparable windows. The reference is built from earlier observations, never from the future.

JSD(P, Q) = ½ KL(P ∥ M) + ½ KL(Q ∥ M)
where M = ½(P + Q)

JSD uses natural logarithms and ranges from 0 to ln(2). Optimal transport uses a fixed, explicit ontology distance matrix between topics, not learned semantic embeddings. Its scale depends on that matrix.

03

Separate surprise from distance

Predictive surprise compares the day's observation with a forecast made using preceding data. Its historical rank is descriptive, not a calibrated probability that a major event occurred.

Insufficient history is displayed as unavailable. Temporal dependence, reporting changes, and model misspecification all limit interpretation.

04

Put evidence before alerts

Candidate signals are prompts for inspection. Coverage warnings can suppress alerts. Events remain traceable within the simulated record, with verification status shown explicitly.

This demo contains invented events and provides no factual sourcing for them. It has no live ingestion, validated probability of crises, or causal attribution.
